title: Replace Map<String, Object> tool results with typed result classes
description:
Tool output schemas are declared via @Tool.Field annotations on the execute() method, but handler methods in BridgeCallbackHandler return Map<String, Object> with string-keyed puts. This means adding a new result key requires updating two places (the handler put() and the tool annotation), and forgetting the annotation is a silent bug that only surfaces at runtime when the specific code path is hit.

This has caused real bugs: get-action-choices-undeclared-action-taken and get-action-choices-undeclared-has-playable-cards, where BridgeCallbackHandler put keys into the result that GetActionChoicesTool didn't declare, causing MCP validation errors that blinded the pilot.

Proposed fix: Replace Map<String, Object> returns with typed result classes per tool. Each tool defines a Result inner class (or standalone class) with typed fields. McpToolRegistry derives the output schema from the class fields via reflection, replacing @Tool.Field annotations. Handler methods populate the typed result directly (result.actionTaken = "..."), so the compiler catches any attempt to set a nonexistent field.

Scope:
- 10 tool classes to convert (3 simple inline ones, 7 that delegate to BridgeCallbackHandler)
- ~226 result.put() calls in BridgeCallbackHandler.java (5473 lines) to convert to typed field assignment
- Shared fields across tools (action_pending, board, game_seq, etc.) could use composition or a shared base class
- McpToolRegistry needs to handle typed result serialization (toMap or Gson reflection)

This is a significant refactor but eliminates an entire class of bugs at compile time.
